name: Theoretical Computer Science

resources.name: Yanofsky. Theoretical Computer Science

resources.name: Anil Ada. Great Ideas in Theoretical Computer Science. CMU

resources.name: O'Donnell. Great Ideas in Theoretical Computer Science. CMU
resources.desc: A series of lectures on selected notable topics in theoretical computer science.

resources.name: Wigderson. Mathematics and Computation: A Theory Revolutionizing Technology and Science

resources.name: Moore & Mertens. The Nature of Computation

resources.name: Atallah & Blanton. Algorithms and Theory of Computation Handbook: General Concepts and Techniques

resources.name: Atallah & Blanton. Algorithms and Theory of Computation Handbook: Special Topics and Techniques
resources.desc: A complete comprehensive encyclopediac handbook which surveys all related areas to theoretical computer science.

resources.name: Handbook of Theoretical Computer Science. Volume A: Algorithms and Complexity
resources.desc: A complete comprehensive encyclopediac handbook which surveys all related areas to theoretical computer science.

resources.name: Handbook of Theoretical Computer Science. Volume B: Formal Methods and Semantics
resources.desc: A complete comprehensive encyclopediac handbook which surveys all related areas to theoretical computer science.

resources.name: Watrous. Introduction to The Theory of Computing
resources.desc: undergrad introduction to theory of computation

resources.name: Intro to Theoretical Computer Science

resources.name: Computability, Complexity & Algorithms. Georgia Institute of Technology
resources.desc: It focuses on the big fundamental questions of computing, and how understanding the power and limitations of algorithms helps us develop the tools to make real-world computers smarter, faster and safer.

resources.name: Sipser. Introduction to Theory of Computation
resources.desc: A standard text for introducing theory of computation for undergrads.

resources.name: Hopcroft, Motwani & Ullman. Introduction to Automata Theory, Languages, and Computation
resources.desc: Introductory undergrad textbook for automata, languages and theory of computation topics.

resources.name: Zhu & Ko. Problem Solving in Automata, Languages, and Complexity
resources.desc: A problem-set text for automata, languages, and complexity.

resources.name: O'Donnell. Graduate Complexity Theory
resources.desc: It covers most of what is believed to be known to get started in complexity theory research.

resources.name: Rudich & Wigderson. Computational Complexity Theory
resources.desc: Three weeks of lectures from the IAS/Park City Mathematics Institute Summer School on computational complexity. Topics include reductions, lower-bounds, average-case complexity, randomness, interactive proof systems, probabilistically checkable proofs, quantum computing, and proof complexity.

resources.name: Arora & Barak. Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach
resources.desc: A golden standard textbook, Surveying computational complexity theory for graduate students and researchers.

resources.name: Goldreich. Computational Complexity: A Conceptual Perspective
resources.desc: A grad introduction to computation complexity theory, emphasizing the idea behind concepts of complexity theory.

resources.name: Goldreich. P, NP, and NP-Completeness: The Basics of Computational Complexity
resources.desc: A very gentle introduction to some fundamental ideas of computational complexity like NP-completeness and P vs NP.

resources.name: Ogihara & Hemaspaandra. The Complexity Theory Companion
resources.desc: An accessible, algorithmically oriented, research-centered, up-to-date guide to some of the most interesting techniques of complexity theory.

resources.name: Papadimitriou. Computational Complexity
resources.desc: Body of knowledge for studying the performance and limitations of computer algorithms. Among topics covered are: reductions and NP-completeness, cryptography and protocols, randomized algorithms, and approximability of optimization problems, circuit complexity, the structural aspects of the P=NP question, parallel computation, and the polynomial hierarchy.

resources.name: Complexity Zoo
resources.desc: a wiki of complexity classes.

resources.name: Mark Bun. CS591 Communication Complexity
resources.desc: A graduate course which introduces the fundamental results and techniques in the area and some research frontier questions. Themes include: Communication models and the communication complexity zoo, Information vs. communication, Query-to-communication lifting, and Applications

resources.name: Rao & Yehudayoff. Communication Complexity and Applications
resources.desc: An excellent and very readable introductory textbook to the field of communication complexity.

resources.name: Jukna. Boolean Function Complexity: Advances and Frontiers
resources.desc: A modern textbook surveying circuit complexity.

resources.name: Clote & Kranakis. Boolean Functions and Computation Models
resources.desc: An introduction to circuit complexity, boolean functions, and computation models.

resources.name: Uni Paderborn. Quantum Complexity Theory. Winter 2020

resources.name: Henry Yuen. The Complexity of Entanglement. Fall 2020
resources.desc: Focuses on cutting edge topics in quantum information that relate to Complexity of Entanglement. - see this class also

resources.name: Robert Robere. Proof Complexity: Algorithms and Lower Bounds

resources.name: Cutland. Computability: An Introduction to Recursive Function Theory
resources.desc: Intuitively, It explains the idea of a computable function: a function whose values can be calculated in an effective or automatic way.

resources.name: Cooper. Computability Theory
resources.desc: A concise, comprehensive, and authoritative introduction to contemporary computability theory, techniques, and results.

resources.name: Davis. Computability and Unsolvability
resources.desc: In this classic text, Dr. Davis provides a clear introduction to computability, at an advanced undergraduate level, that serves the needs of specialists and non-specialists alike.

resources.name: Soare. Recursively Enumerable Sets and Degree
resources.desc: It gives a complete account of the theory of r.e degrees. The definitions, results and proofs are always clearly motivated and explained before the formal presentation; the proofs are described with remarkable clarity and conciseness.

resources.name: Odifreddi. Classical Recursion Theory: The Theory of Functions and Sets of Natural Numbers
resources.desc: An impressive presentation of classical recursion theory. It is highly recommended to everyone interested in recursion theory.

resources.name: Copeland, Posy & Shagrir (editors). Computability: Turing, Gödel, Church, and Beyond

resources.name: Pudlák. Logical Foundations of Mathematics and Computational Complexity: A Gentle Introduction
resources.desc: Presents a wide range of results in logic and computational complexity.

resources.name: Cambridge Foundations of CS

resources.name: Pierce. Software Foundations. Pennsylvania

resources.name: UW CSE505 18au Principles of PL
resources.desc: Techniques for thinking crisply about programming languages, write some fascinating programs, and discuss various design tradeoffs.

resources.name: Chlipala. Formal Reasoning About Programs

resources.name: Lean Proof Assistant

resources.name: Martin-Löf. Intuitionistic Type Theory

resources.desc: The present book is intended as a first systematic exposition of the basics of univalent foundations, and a collection of examples of this new style of reasoning — but without requiring the reader to know or learn any formal logic, or to use any computer proof assistant.

resources.name: Helsinki. Haskell MOOC
resources.desc: An online course on functional programming with Haskell programming language, and a live interactive Telegram community.

resources.name: Cornell. Functional Programming in Ocaml
resources.desc: A modern course on data structures and functional programming using OCaml.

resources.name: Demaine/Ku/Soloman. Introduction to Algorithms. MIT
resources.desc: A first course on basic algorithms and data structures. — added by Erik himself!

resources.name: Demaine/Devadas/Lynch. Design and Analysis of algorithms. MIT
resources.desc: A second course on algorithms and data structures. — added by Erik himself!

resources.name: Erik Demaine. Advanced Data Structures. MIT
resources.desc: It covers major results and current directions of research in data structure.

resources.name: Arora. Advanced Algorithm Design
resources.desc: Notably uses ideas such as randomness, approximation, high dimensional geometry. Faces uncertainty, approaches to handle big data, handling intractability, heuristic approaches, ..etc.

resources.name: Knuth. The Art of Computer Programming
resources.desc: A legendary series by Donald Knuth on design and analysis of algorithms.

resources.name: Demaine. Algorithmic Lower Bounds: Fun with Hardness Proofs
resources.desc: A class taking a practical approach to proving problems can't be solved efficient.

resources.name: Demaine, Gasarch & Hajiaghayi. Computers and Intractability: A Guide to Algorithmic Lower Bounds
resources.desc: A sequel to Garey and Johnson's Computers and Intractability: A Guide to NP-Completeness. resources.name: Demaine. Games, Puzzles, and Computation
resources.desc: It shows that games and puzzles can serve as powerful models of computation, Offering a new way of thinking about computation.

resources.name: Mary Wootters. Randomized Algorithms and Probabilistic Analysis. Stanford
resources.desc: Key tools of probabilistic analysis, and application of these tools to understand the behaviors of random processes and algorithms. Emphasis is on theoretical foundations, though applications will be discussed in machine learning and data analysis, networking, and systems. Topics include tail bounds, the probabilistic method, Markov chains, and martingales, with applications to analyzing random graphs, metric embeddings, and random walks.

resources.name: Koutsoupias. Probability and Computing. Oxford
resources.desc: Introduction to probabilistic methods in computer science.

resources.name: Lee. Randomized Algorithms and Probabilistic Analysis. Washington.
resources.desc: Topics include Discrete probability, High-dimensional geometry and statistics, Information and entropy, and Markov chains and convergence to equilibrium.

resources.name: Aspnes. Notes on Randomized Algorithms

resources.name: Chekuri. Approximation Algorithmis Illinois

resources.name: Dinitz. Approximation Algorithms. Johns Hopkins

resources.name: Gupta & Ravi. Approximation Algorithms. CMU
resources.desc: It includes convex programming-based, randomness, and metric methods.

resources.name: Williamson & Shmoys. The Design of Approximation Algorithms

resources.name: Du & Ko. Design and Analysis of Approximation Algorithms

Parametarized Algorithms by Warsaw

resources.name: Lindell. Tutorials on the Foundations of Cryptography
resources.desc: Advanced tutorials appropriate for self-study by experienced researchers,

resources.name: Goldreich. Modern Cryptography, Probabilistic Proofs and Pseudorandomness

resources.name: MAISI

resources.name: Telgarsky. Deep Learning Theory. Illinois

resources.name: Vaughan. CS260: Machine Learning Theory
resources.desc: A broad overview of the theoretical foundations underlying common machine learning algorithms.

resources.name: Livni. COS 511 Theoretical Machine Learning. Princeton
resources.desc: Formally define and study various models that have been proposed for learning. The course will present and contrast the statistical, computational and online models for learning. We will present and rigorously analyze some of the most successful algorithms in machine learning that are extensively used today.

resources.name: Moitra. Theoretical Foundations for Deep Learning. MIT
resources.desc: It explores theoretical foundations for deep learning, emphasizing the following themes: (1) Approximation: What sorts of functions can be represented by deep networks, and does depth provably increase the expressive power? (2) Optimization: Essentially all optimization problems we want to solve in practice are non-convex. What frameworks can be used to analyze such problems? (3) Beyond-Worst Case Analysis: Deep networks can memorize worst-case data, so why do they generalize well on real-world data?

resources.name: Arora. Overcoming Intractability in Machine Learning
resources.desc: A seminar course that will focus on the following phenomenon: many problems in machine learning are formally intractable (e.g., NP-hard). Nevertheless they are solved in practice by heuristics. Can we design algorithms with provable guarantees (running time, solution quality)?

resources.name: Vazirani & Kearns. An Introduction to Computational Learning Theory
resources.desc: Emphasizing issues of computational efficiency, It introduces a number of central topics in computational learning theory.

resources.name: Shalev-Shwartz. Understanding Machine Learning: From Theory to Algorithms

resources.name: Tim Roughgarden. Complexity Theory, Game Theory, and Economics: The Barbados Lectures
resources.desc: A mini-course notes of two-fold goals: mini-course is twofold: (i) Explain how complexity theory has helped illuminate several barriers in economics and game theory; and (ii) Illustrate how game-theoretic questions have led to new and interesting complexity theory, including recent several breakthroughs.

resources.name: Eva Tardos. Algorithmic Game Theory
resources.desc: It combines algorithmic thinking with game-theoretic, or, more generally, economic concepts. The course will study a range of topics at this interface. The only prerequisite to the course is mathematical thinking.

resources.name: Chekuri. Topics in Algorithms: Algorithmic Game Theory
resources.desc: A broad graduate-level introduction to: auctions, existence and computation of equilibria in games and markets, algorithmic mechanism design, price of anarchy and price of stability, games relevant to networks and e-commerce. The emphasis will be on conceptual ideas and algorithmic aspects. No familiarity with game theory or economics will be assumed.

resources.name: Penna. Algorithmic Game Theory
resources.desc: The course discusses algorithmic aspects of game theory, such as a general introduction to game theory, auctions, mechanisms, the costs of a central control optimum versus those of an equilibrium under selfish agents, and algorithms and complexity of computing equilibria.

resources.name: Brown. Resources list for game theory

resources.name: Xu. Topics in Learning and Game Theory

resources.name: Eva Tardos & et.al. Algorithmic Game Theory

resources.name: Aho & Ullman. Foundations of Computer Science
